## Planned changes for future releases

- Experiment with extending the treatment knock-out (trtKO) functionality into a likelihood-ratio test for hypothesis testing. Update the tutorial on customizing statistical analyses, if needed. 
- Autodetect fixed-effect type, e.g., fixed-effect columns of R type "character" or "factor" are treated as two-level categorical factors, and numeric columns are treated as discrete additive effects (e.g., like a time series). Will need to update the <span class = "gene">RORB</span> tutorial and any other tutorials which discuss time-series modeling. 
- Ensure any columns flagged as a time series are also treated as fixed-effects. 
- Add a check during the fit to see if any transition points can be replaced with a slope.
- Add variable check to the loading of <span class = "code_variable">plot.settings</span> in <span class = "function">wisp</span>. Currently only runs <span class = "function">check_list</span> without doing a more substantive check. Compare with the more detailed checks of <span class = "code_variable">MCMC.settings</span>.
- Allow <span class = "code_variable">MCMC.prior</span> to be a vector of different prior distributions for each parameter. When completed, update the tutorial on customizing statistical analyses.
- Ensure nested loops for matrix operations have the major axis (column) on outside. 
- Extracellular (out-of-soma) transcripts do not follow a Poisson distribution, and so any attempt to model them with wisp needs to account for this. 

## Version 2.6.0 (October 29, 2026)

- **Breaking API change**: the eight dotted plotting functions (<span class = "function">plot.ratecount</span>, <span class = "function">plot.timeseries</span>, <span class = "function">plot.parameters</span>, <span class = "function">plot.effect.dist</span>, <span class = "function">plot.species.summary</span>, <span class = "function">plot.MCMC.walks</span>, <span class = "function">plot.decomposition</span>, <span class = "function">plot.MCMC.bs.comparison</span>) have been removed. They looked like S3 methods but never were one, since <span class = "function">wisp()</span> used to return a plain, unclassed list, so <span class = "function">plot()</span> could never dispatch to them; users had to call each by its full dotted name. <span class = "function">wisp()</span> now classes its return value <span class = "code_variable">"wisp"</span>, and all plotting goes through one real, exported S3 method, <span class = "function">plot.wisp</span>, selected with a <span class = "code_variable">type</span> argument. All other arguments to each old function are unchanged and are simply passed through <span class = "code_variable">...</span>. The old-name to new-call mapping is:
  - <span class = "function">plot.ratecount(model, ...)</span> &rarr; <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "ratecount", ...)</span>
  - <span class = "function">plot.timeseries(model, ...)</span> &rarr; <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "timeseries", ...)</span>
  - <span class = "function">plot.parameters(model, ...)</span> &rarr; <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "parameters", ...)</span>
  - <span class = "function">plot.effect.dist(model, ...)</span> &rarr; <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "effect.dist", ...)</span>
  - <span class = "function">plot.species.summary(model, ...)</span> &rarr; <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "species.summary", ...)</span>
  - <span class = "function">plot.MCMC.walks(model, ...)</span> &rarr; <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "MCMC.walks", ...)</span>
  - <span class = "function">plot.decomposition(model, ...)</span> &rarr; <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "decomposition", ...)</span>
  - <span class = "function">plot.MCMC.bs.comparison(model, ...)</span> &rarr; <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "MCMC.bs.comparison", ...)</span>
- <span class = "function">plot.wisp</span>'s <span class = "code_variable">print.plots</span>, <span class = "code_variable">verbose</span>, and <span class = "code_variable">species</span> arguments, previously only available by name on the underlying per-type functions (and so only reachable through <span class = "code_variable">...</span>), are now named formals on <span class = "function">plot.wisp</span> itself: <span class = "function">plot.wisp(x, type, print.plots = TRUE, verbose = TRUE, species = "all", decompose = FALSE, ...)</span>. Two of these are **breaking changes**:
  - <span class = "code_variable">print.plots</span> now defaults to <span class = "code_variable">TRUE</span> at the <span class = "function">plot.wisp</span> level (every underlying function's own old default was <span class = "code_variable">FALSE</span>). A call that relied on the old default to stay silent (e.g. in a script or non-interactive context) must now pass <span class = "code_variable">print.plots = FALSE</span> explicitly to keep the old behavior.
  - <span class = "code_variable">species</span> now defaults to the string <span class = "code_variable">"all"</span> (translated internally to <span class = "code_variable">c()</span>) rather than <span class = "code_variable">c()</span> directly; this is purely a more readable public spelling of the same default and changes nothing about which species are plotted. <span class = "code_variable">species</span> is only forwarded to <span class = "code_variable">type \%in\% c("ratecount", "timeseries", "parameters", "species.summary")</span> (the types whose underlying function actually has a <span class = "code_variable">species</span> argument); passing a non-default <span class = "code_variable">species</span> for any other <span class = "code_variable">type</span> now raises a warning and is otherwise ignored, rather than erroring with "unused argument" or being silently (and confusingly) absorbed by <span class = "code_variable">...</span>.
  - <span class = "code_variable">verbose</span> defaults to <span class = "code_variable">TRUE</span>, matching every underlying function's own existing default, so this is not a behavior change.
- **Breaking API change**: <span class = "code_variable">type = "decomposition"</span> has been removed as a standalone <span class = "function">plot.wisp</span> type and folded into <span class = "code_variable">type = "ratecount"</span> as a display mode, selected with a new <span class = "code_variable">decompose</span> argument. <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "decomposition", species = "X", ...)</span> becomes <span class = "function">plot(model, type = "ratecount", species = "X", decompose = TRUE, ...)</span>. As before, <span class = "code_variable">decompose = TRUE</span> requires <span class = "code_variable">species</span> to resolve to exactly one species level (not <span class = "code_variable">"all"</span>, not a multi-element vector), or a clear error is raised; setting <span class = "code_variable">decompose = TRUE</span> for any <span class = "code_variable">type</span> other than <span class = "code_variable">"ratecount"</span> is also an error. Unlike the old standalone type, the decomposed rate-count plots now honor the dispatcher's shared <span class = "code_variable">print.plots</span> and <span class = "code_variable">verbose</span> arguments, just like every other type.
- Added five new, real, dispatchable S3 methods for the <span class = "code_variable">"wisp"</span> class, for the same reason <span class = "function">plot.wisp</span> was made a real S3 method in the breaking change above (plain <span class = "function">exportPattern</span>-based registration is not reliably found by dispatch once <span class = "function">colorspace</span>, a <span class = "code_variable">Depends:</span> of this package, turns a base generic into an S4 generic for the session -- so each of these also carries an explicit <span class = "code_variable">@method</span> roxygen tag and an explicit <span class = "function">S3method()</span> <span class = "code_variable">NAMESPACE</span> entry):
  - <span class = "function">print.wisp(x, ...)</span>: terse console digest of a fitted model (parameter count, grouping levels, resampling method/counts, and a stats summary).
  - <span class = "function">summary.wisp(object, ...)</span> / <span class = "function">print.summary.wisp(x, ...)</span>: <span class = "function">summary()</span> returns an object of class <span class = "code_variable">"summary.wisp"</span> wrapping <span class = "code_variable">object$stats$parameters</span> plus model-size/fit-setting context; <span class = "function">print()</span> formats it for console display.
  - <span class = "function">residuals.wisp(object, type = c("raw", "log"), ...)</span>: returns the residual summary statistics (by group) computed during the fit, for either raw residuals or log-residuals.
  - <span class = "function">coef.wisp(object, ...)</span>: returns the fitted parameter estimates as a plain named numeric vector, per the usual R <span class = "function">coef()</span> convention.
  - <span class = "function">confint.wisp(object, parm = NULL, level = 0.95, ...)</span>: returns the already-computed confidence intervals (stored at whatever <span class = "code_variable">alpha</span> was used when <span class = "function">sample.stats</span> last ran, default 95%) directly when <span class = "code_variable">level = 0.95</span>; for any other <span class = "code_variable">level</span>, transparently re-runs <span class = "function">sample.stats</span> (cheaply -- it only re-quantiles the already-stored resampled parameters, without refitting) to recompute at the requested level.
  - All five give a clear, specific error (or message) rather than a cryptic one when called on a model fit with <span class = "code_variable">fit_only = TRUE</span> (i.e. no statistical analysis was ever run).
- Renamed the two exported warping/sigmoid math utilities <span class = "function">wisp.warp</span> and <span class = "function">wisp.sigmoid</span> to <span class = "function">wisp_warp</span> and <span class = "function">wisp_sigmoid</span> (dot to underscore). This is a pure rename with no change to arguments or behavior; it removes the last two function names in the package that looked like (but never were) S3 methods for a <span class = "code_variable">wisp</span> generic (<span class = "function">wisp()</span> is the model-fitting function itself, not a generic, and never will be one).

## Version 2.5.1 (October 3, 2026)

- Updated .Rbuildignore.

## Version 2.5 (October 3, 2026) 

- Improved time series parsing.
- Updated time series plots to allow for tertiary effects.

## Version 2.4 (July 3, 2026)

- Part 2 of a major code refactor/optimization. 
- Finished refactoring wspc object class and its initialization method into a more organized structure.
- Fixed issue in <span class = "function">extrapolate_none</span>.
- Added option to level preprocessing coordinate transform (the <span class = "function">cortical_coordinate_transform</span> function) based on different layers.
- Updated Roxygen2 descriptions for user-facing R functions. 
- Checked all tutorials to ensure they work with current version and removed auto-dating, so their current working version is properly documented. Included footnotes on saved and pre-processed code chunks. 
- Substantial code cleaning. 

## Version 2.3 (June 16, 2026)

- Part 1 of a major code refactor/optimization. 
- Improved algorithm in <span class = "function">check_parameter_feasibility</span> for finding nearby feasible initial parameters.
- Improved placement of <span class = "function">check_parameter_feasibility</span> within the various fit, MCMC, and bootstrap pipelines.
- Converted several large-signature stand-alone functions into wspc methods: <span class = "function">compute_gamma_dispersion</span>, <span class = "function">make_extrapolation_pool</span>, <span class = "function">find_count_log_means</span>, <span class = "function">estimate_change_points</span>, and <span class = "function">estimate_initial_parameters</span>. 
- Simplified parameter vector handling. 
- Wrote checks into tutorials, to ensure code changes do not change results. 
- Replaced some R Lists with std::vector.
- Improved weight-matrix construction.
- Replaced pcg with std rng, to ease licensing issues.
- Removed stan variables from wspc objects.
- Replaced R-style masking with numeric indexing for summed count data. 
- Added <span class = "code_variable">print.settings</span> argument <span class = "code_variable">splitting_factor_colors</span> to <span class = "function">wisp</span> to allow users to specify colors for the splitting factor in ratecount and timeseries plots. 
- Performed extensive optimization of the code, leading to a x2 or x3 speedup in running <span class = "function">wisp</span>. 
- Documentation updated, but not yet rebuilt. 

## Version 2.2 (June 5, 2026)

- Added <span class = "code_variable">model.settings</span> argument <span class = "code_variable">max_bin</span> to <span class = "function">wisp</span> which allows users to specify the largest bin number. If left at zero, the function will infer the maximum bin number from the count data.
- Aligned matrix nested loops to major axis (column) to improve computational efficiency.
- Updated <span class = "function">plot.decomposition</span> to allow for multiple contexts. 
- Fixed <span class = "function">plot.timeseries</span> to plot single-block species. 
- Added LRO parameter grid search option. (Very effective!)
- Updated preprocessing functions for making count data. 
- Fixed batch size for forking. 

## Version 2.1 (March 1, 2026)

- Added <span class = "code_variable">model.settings</span> argument <span class = "code_variable">trtKO</span> to <span class = "function">wisp</span> which enables excluding treatments to run reduced models. 
- Replaced corrupted data file "corticallaminar_model.rds" with working version (hopefully for the last time!).
- Fixed memory leak related to CI computation. 

## Version 2.0 (Feb 19, 2026)

- Release attached to NAR resubmission.
- Redesigned plots.
- Added attractor simulation functionality and benchmarking.
- Includes first-draft versions of package tutorials.
- Note that the package data file "corticallaminar_model.rds" was corrupted and should be pulled from the latest version or latest commit on the main branch. 

## Version 1.1

- Added discrete time-series modeling functionality (the <span class = "code_variable">timeseries</span> variable option) and plotting (the function <span class = "function">plot.timeseries</span>).
- Ensured code would robustly run for any data including at least <span class = "code_variable">count</span> and <span class = "code_variable">bin</span> columns, without need for <span class = "code_variable">context</span>, <span class = "code_variable">species</span>, <span class = "code_variable">ran</span>, or fixed-effect variables. 
- Added explicit <span class = "code_variable">fit_only</span> option to <span class = "function">wisp</span> to avoid running any parameter estimation (MCMC or bootstrapping). 

## Version 1.0

- Initial public release of wispack, as used in [this preprint](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.06.11.659209).
- Defines the <span class = "function">wisp</span> function for implementing wisps. 
- Introduces one-dimensional warped sigmoidal Poisson-process mixed-effect modeling (one-dimensional wisps) for testing for functional spatial effects in spatial transcriptomics data.
